supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS proxy requests from WS-BCARTER-01 are attributable to ChartMate's cmupdate.exe process. The process was started from Ben Carter's AppData\Local\ChartMate directory, and matching process/network records show requests at about five-minute intervals from 13:38 through 14:08 UTC.

The requested endpoint is update.chartmate-imaging.net, whereas the inventory lists update.chartmate-imaging.com as the approved updater endpoint. The endpoint difference is an unresolved anomaly, not proof of maliciousness.

The observed updater path under the user's AppData directory differs from the inventory's approved ChartMate path under Program Files; Sysmon also records a file-create event targeting the running cmupdate.exe file.

Some requests to the .net endpoint failed at the proxy (407 and 502), while other requests succeeded with status 200; these records do not establish what content, if any, was transferred inside the HTTPS tunnels.

At 13:54 UTC, WS-BCARTER-01 connected to FILE-HD-01 over SMB, and FILE-HD-01 logged an ANONYMOUS LOGON network session. The available records do not show which share or resources, if any, were accessed.

The evidence does not establish malicious activity: the periodic requests are associated with an updater-like process and fit the approximate cadence described for ChartMate, but its endpoint and executable location do not match the supplied inventory.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy CONNECT records identify the requested hostname and tunnel outcome, but the supplied records do not show the HTTPS request or response contents.
The records do not include a hash, signature-validation result, or other provenance evidence for cmupdate.exe.
The SMB records show a connection and an anonymous logon, but not share access, file operations, or transferred data.
The supplied evidence does not include an authoritative confirmation of whether the .net hostname or the AppData installation is legitimate for this organization.
claims_not_established: Whether update.chartmate-imaging.net is an authorized ChartMate endpoint or an impersonating or otherwise unauthorized endpoint.
Whether cmupdate.exe is genuine, signed by the expected publisher, or has been modified.
Whether the file-create event reflects a legitimate updater self-replacement or an unauthorized change.
Whether the HTTPS tunnels delivered an update, other content, or no meaningful content.
Whether the anonymous SMB session accessed any share or data.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire cmupdate.exe and verify its hash, signature, publisher, file metadata, and provenance; compare it with a known-good ChartMate installer.
Confirm with the software owner or vendor whether update.chartmate-imaging.net and the per-user AppData installation are legitimate.
Review proxy and endpoint telemetry with TLS inspection or equivalent visibility, if available, to determine the content and destination details of successful tunnels.
Collect FILE-HD-01 SMB share-access and file-operation logs around 13:54 UTC to determine whether the anonymous session accessed resources.
Check endpoint file-integrity, installation, and update logs to identify what changed at 13:38 UTC.
